description: Add `mo notify setup` guided CLI command that probes Hermes webhook readiness, generates one shared secret, writes the Mohist outbound Hermes config directly to ~/.mohist/config.jsonc, and prints a copy-pasteable `hermes webhook subscribe mohist` command carrying the same secret.

tasks.title: Implement `mo notify setup` guided CLI command
tasks.spec: specs/notify-setup/spec.md#Probe Hermes webhook readiness before changing any config
tasks.description: Add a new `notify` command group with a `setup` subcommand to the Mohist CLI, registered alongside existing groups in MohistCliCommands.Build (packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/MohistCliCommands.cs). The command: (1) probes the Hermes webhook health endpoint (default http://127.0.0.1:8644/health, overridable via --health-base / --webhook-url) using a throwaway HttpRequestMessage with a short explicit timeout, modeled on OtelCommands.RunStatusAsync's friendly-no-stack-trace discipline; on HttpRequestException, TaskCanceledException, or non-success status it prints a clear 'Hermes webhook platform is not started' message pointing at docs/hermes-notifications.md, writes nothing, and returns non-zero. (2) On probe success, generates one random secret via RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(32) rendered as base64url. (3) Derives the webhook receiver URL from the probed base by appending /webhooks/mohist (overridable via --webhook-url), then writes Mohist.Notifications.Hermes { WebhookUrl, Secret, EnabledTypes=[approval_requested, workflow_failed, issue_completed] } directly to ~/.mohist/config.jsonc via JsonNode round-trip using IFileSystem (not through mo config set / the flat ConfigService schema). Carries a CLI-local copy of the JSONC comment-strip routine (the server helper lives in the server assembly; the CLI must not take a server-package dependency). Prompts y/N (default no) before overwriting any existing Hermes value; on EOF/non-interactive stdin it aborts and writes nothing rather than hanging. Seeds the full Mohist.Notifications.Hermes structure if the file does not exist. (4) Prints a complete `hermes webhook subscribe mohist --deliver <platform> --deliver-only --secret <same-secret> --prompt '{message}'` command with inline {message} passthrough (no --prompt-file), reflecting --platform when given and placeholder guidance when omitted; the --secret value is byte-identical to the written config value (same string literal). (5) Prints `mo update server` reload guidance after a successful write. The command must NOT fork or invoke hermes and must NOT touch any Hermes-side file.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo notify setup --help` exits 0 and documents the --health-base, --webhook-url, and --platform options.
When the Hermes health endpoint responds successfully, the command proceeds to generate a secret, write Mohist config, and print the subscribe command (exit 0).

When the health endpoint is unreachable (connection refused), times out, or returns a non-success status, the command prints a clear 'Hermes webhook platform is not started' message that references the Hermes notification docs, writes NO Mohist configuration, exits non-zero, and emits no stack trace (no 'Connection refused' / socket exception text).
No secret is generated and no config is written when the probe fails (verified via FakeFileSystem having no writes).

The secret written into Mohist config under Mohist:Notifications:Hermes:Secret is byte-for-byte identical to the --secret value in the printed Hermes subscribe command (same string literal, asserted in spec).

On a fresh config (no existing Mohist:Notifications:Hermes values), the command writes the derived WebhookUrl (base + /webhooks/mohist), the generated secret, and EnabledTypes containing exactly approval_requested, workflow_failed, and issue_completed.
When one or more Mohist:Notifications:Hermes values already exist, the command prompts the user (y/N) before overwriting and does NOT silently overwrite; declining writes nothing.
When stdin is at EOF / non-interactive, the command aborts without writing and without hanging.
After a successful write, the command prints guidance to reload via `mo update server`.
With --platform telegram, the printed subscribe command includes --deliver telegram, --deliver-only, the exact generated --secret, and inline --prompt '{message}'; it does NOT use --prompt-file.
Without --platform, the printed subscribe command omits a concrete --deliver value and prints guidance that the user must supply the target delivery platform.
The command does not spawn, fork, or exec any hermes process (FakeCommandExecutor records no hermes invocation).
The only file the command writes is ~/.mohist/config.jsonc; no Hermes-side config or subscription file is created, edited, or deleted (FakeFileSystem asserts the single written path).

Unit: the CLI-local JSONC comment-strip helper strips // line comments and /* */ block comments while preserving string literals (including escaped quotes) verbatim, matching the server StripJsoncComments behavior over the stable JSONC subset.
`dotnet build` of the CLI project succeeds with warnings-as-errors (the repo's C# lint gate).

The new CLI spec tests (CliNotifySetupCommandSpecs) pass and cover: help listing, probe-down abort (non-zero, no config written, no stack trace), fresh-config write with correct defaults, overwrite-confirmation (accept + decline), non-interactive stdin abort, shared-secret identity between config and printed command, --platform deliver shape, no-platform placeholder shape, no hermes fork, and single-file write constraint.
`npm test` (repo server test gate, which includes TreatWarningsAsErrors) continues to pass.
tasks.output: packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/MohistCliCommands.Notify.cs (new command group + setup subcommand + CLI-local JSONC strip helper + Hermes subscribe command renderer), registration in packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/MohistCliCommands.cs (root.Subcommands.Add of the notify group), and packages/cli/tests/Mohist.Cli.Tests/CliNotifySetupCommandSpecs.cs (spec coverage for all scenarios).
tasks.notes: Prerequisite #350 (outbound Hermes engine + Mohist:Notifications:Hermes config schema) is already in stage 'done', so the config section this command populates already exists and is bound server-side by HermesNotificationOptions — no schema change is needed. Design decisions D1-D8 in design.md are all internal steps of this single command flow and are intentionally bundled per the task-splitting guidance (no cross-platform abstraction, no explicitly independent component, no large prerequisite refactor). Follow existing command-group patterns: OtelCommands (probe discipline) and ConfigProvidersCommands (Build registration). Use IFileSystem so tests inject FakeFileSystem; use the MohistCliApi.Output/Error/StandardInput for all I/O. The health probe target is an absolute external URL, so construct a throwaway HttpRequestMessage rather than reusing api.Http (whose BaseAddress points at the Mohist server).
